newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shell Singapore cuts runs, plans maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Shell Singapore cuts runs, plans maintenance.

text.p: Shell Singapore has cut crude runs to 50,000 tonne per day (TPD) at its 59,000-TPD (435,000-barrel-per-day) refinery following poor margins and high stocks, a Shell spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
She also said that the company has scheduled a one-week maintenance for its No 4 115,000-bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) beginning on July 6.
The spokeswoman said the crude run cuts will be maintained "subject to market condition."
Trading sources said that the cuts were expected due to high middle distillate stocks in Singapore which had led to a big drop in the price of gas oil.
The lower product prices against a firm crude market has squeezed refining margins, currently in the red, they said.
Industry sources said that Exxon Singapore has also cut crude runs by about 10 percent since late last month but this was not confirmed by Exxon officials.
